title: Next-session request
description: The body of the next-session request: the request that qory sends to the control plane after a session of the run ended, to ask for the next session. It is an object of session, state and reason, with no verdict. The control plane ignores a member that this schema does not define, such as verdict, unless the must_understand of the request lists it. The control plane reads the newest verdict that the run stored after the previous step, and the rules by which it picks the next session from that verdict are the control plane's, not this schema's. When the session's type_settings turn on a check that runs after the session, and it fails, qory stores that check's result before it sends this request. So the control plane reads the newest verdict after that result. State and reason follow the rules of dev.qory.session.exited that do not depend on its exit_code: a cancelled session has a reason; the reasons timeout and interrupted are for a cancelled session only; and the reason gateway_lost is for a failed session only. qory sends the request after each session that did not pause, and only for a run whose run documents have shared_run true. The answer is next-session-answer.schema.json. qory sends the request through Forager's link, and the gateway forwards it to the control plane. A container cannot send it.

session.description: Forager's number of the session that ended, from 1: the session of its dev.qory.session.exited, https://qory.dev/contracts/forager/v1/events/session.exited.schema.json.

state.description: How the session ended, the state of its dev.qory.session.exited: succeeded, failed or cancelled. A session that paused has no request: qory closes the run as paused.

reason.description: Why the session ended, the reason of its dev.qory.session.exited, or null when that event has none.

must_understand.description: The members of the document that the reader must understand, each as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) counted from the document, such as /state. List each once, at most 32. A pointer has no line feed, and writes ~ only as ~0 or ~1. Each pointer is to a member that this schema defines. The control plane ignores a member that this schema does not define, unless must_understand lists it. It refuses a request whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define, 400 invalid_request.
